instructions:
1. Lie face down on a bench set to about 45 degrees with a dumbbell in each hand and arms hanging straight down.
2. Keep your chest pressed to the bench and your head neutral.
3. Pull the dumbbells toward your ribs, flaring your elbows out and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Lower the dumbbells under control until your arms hang straight.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with your elbows and drive them up and back to hit the rear delts.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
3. Keep your chest down and do not lift your torso off the bench.
4. Use a controlled tempo instead of swinging the weights.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand and arms hanging straight down, palms facing each other.
2. Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
3. Raise the dumbbells out to your sides until your arms are level with your torso.
4. Lower the dumbbells under control to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with your elbows, not your hands, to target the rear delts.
2. Keep your neck neutral and your chest on the bench.
3. Pause briefly at the top and squeeze the rear delts.
4. Use light weight and a slow tempo to avoid swinging.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand and arms hanging down by your sides, palms facing forward.
2. Keep your upper arms still against your sides.
3. Curl the dumbbells up by bending your elbows, supinating so your palms face you.
4. Lower the dumbbells under control until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms fixed and only move your forearms.
2. Let the dumbbells fully stretch the biceps at the bottom.
3. Supinate the wrist fully for a stronger peak contraction.
4. Use a controlled tempo with no momentum.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended over your chest, palms facing each other.
2. Keep your upper arms vertical and still.
3. Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells toward the sides of your head.
4. Extend your elbows to press the dumbbells back up until your arms are straight.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms fixed and only move your forearms.
2. Lower under control to feel the stretch in the triceps.
3. Keep your wrists neutral throughout.
4. Tuck your elbows in rather than letting them flare wide.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back on the floor with knees bent and feet flat.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended over your chest, palms facing each other.
3. Keep your upper arms still and bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells toward the sides of your head.
4. Stop when your upper arms touch the floor.
5. Extend your elbows to press the dumbbells back up until your arms are straight.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms fixed and only move your forearms.
2. Use the floor to limit the range and protect your elbows.
3. Keep your wrists neutral throughout.
4. Control the lowering phase instead of dropping the weights.
